$comment: Role registry (implementer-neutral). The ESPD role model: the buyer types that create a Request and the economic-operator roles that create a Response, each with the mandatory/optional disposition of the four exclusion-ground categories, plus the Part III section-code prefix -> exclusion-category map. EO roles additionally carry an `xmlMapping` (cac:EconomicOperatorParty/cac:EconomicOperatorRole/cbc:RoleCode = <EoRoleType code>), which the Part II section A mapping serialises. The BUYER types carry NO xmlMapping: in ESPD-EDM 5.0.0 the buyer/EO split is STRUCTURAL (a Request's cac:ContractingParty vs a Response's cac:EconomicOperatorParty), and there is no grounded serialization for the Contracting-Authority vs Contracting-Entity sub-distinction (cbc:PartyTypeCode has no ESPD codelist and no Schematron rule). The two buyer types are kept so the CA/CE regulatory distinction (Directive 2014/24 vs 2014/25) survives in the model. Display text, and which Parts a UI shows or makes editable per role, are presentation: they live in the consuming application (the demo's role-ui.json), keyed by role id. The dispositions below were reviewed (the question was whether Art. 80(1) of Directive 2014/25/EU makes some categories conditional for contracting entities) and confirmed by the ESPD team: see status and statusNote.
statusNote: The exclusion-ground dispositions are confirmed by the ESPD team: all four categories are mandatory for both buyer types (contracting authority and contracting entity) and for every economic-operator role.

exclusionCategoryMap.$comment: Maps a Part III exclusion-ground section-code PREFIX to its exclusion category. Longest-match-independent: prefixes are mutually exclusive. 'exg-sitn' (conflicts of interest / distortion situations) rolls up to 'misconduct'.
